title: Idempotents of B/IB lift after an etale neighbourhood of V(I)
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, $A\to B$ a ring map with $B$ integral over $A$, and $\bar e\in B/IB$ an idempotent. Then there exist a ring map $A\to A'$ such that $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and the induced map $\alpha:A/I\to A'/IA'$ is an isomorphism, and an idempotent $e'\in B\otimes_AA'$ lifting $\bar e$: the composite $B\otimes_AA'\to B\otimes_A(A'/IA')\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}_B\otimes\alpha^{-1}}B\otimes_A(A/I)=B/IB$ maps $e'$ to $\bar e$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07M4 (lemma-lift-idempotent-upstairs) and its proof (uses Lemma lemma-helper-integral, Lemma lemma-lift-factorization-easy, Lemma lemma-separate-image-closed-from-closed, Algebra Lemmas Tag 00GU, 00HZ and lemma-disjoint-decomposition); the precise meaning of 'lifting' (via the isomorphism $A/I\cong A'/IA'$) is made explicit by the agent

proof.text: *An annihilating polynomial.* Choose $y\in B$ lifting $\bar e$. Since $B$ is integral over $A$ and the image of $y$ in $B/IB$ is the idempotent $\bar e$, there are $d\ge1$ and a monic $f\in A[x]$ with $f(y)=0$ in $B$ and $f\equiv x^d(x-1)^d$ modulo $I$ [lem-weil-pbc-integral-idempotent-annihilating-polynomial].

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M4 (lemma-lift-idempotent-upstairs), first two sentences (Lemma Tag 09XG)

proof.text: *Lifting the factorization.* In $(A/I)[x]$ we have $\bar f=\bar g\bar h$ with $\bar g=x^d$ and $\bar h=(x-1)^d$. The leading coefficient of $\bar g$ is $1$, a unit, and $\bar g,\bar h$ generate the unit ideal: $1=(x-(x-1))^{2d-1}=\sum_{i=0}^{2d-1}\binom{2d-1}{i}x^i(-(x-1))^{2d-1-i}$, and in each term $i\ge d$ or $2d-1-i\ge d$, so each term lies in $(x^d)+((x-1)^d)$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-lift-coprime-factorization-etale] gives a ring map $A\to A_1$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A_1\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and $\alpha_1:A/I\to A_1/IA_1$ an isomorphism, and $g,h\in A_1[x]$ with $f=gh$ in $A_1[x]$, $g\equiv x^d$ and $h\equiv(x-1)^d$ modulo $IA_1$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M4 (lemma-lift-idempotent-upstairs), third sentence (Lemma Tag 07M1); the coprimality of $x^d$ and $(x-1)^d$, which Stacks leaves implicit, is written out

proof.text: *Replacing $A$ by $A_1$.* Put $B_1=B\otimes_AA_1$; it is integral over $A_1$ [lem-weil-pbc-integral-base-change]. The map $B\to B_1$, $b\mapsto b\otimes1$, induces $B/IB=B\otimes_A(A/I)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}\otimes\alpha_1}B\otimes_A(A_1/IA_1)=B_1/IB_1$, an isomorphism; let $\bar e_1$ be the image of $\bar e$, an idempotent of $B_1/IB_1$. Then $y_1=y\otimes1$ lifts $\bar e_1$, and $f(y_1)=0$ since $f$ has coefficients in $A$. Set $b_1=g(y_1)$, $b_2=h(y_1)\in B_1$. Then $b_1b_2=(gh)(y_1)=f(y_1)=0$; modulo $IB_1$, $b_1\equiv\bar e_1^d=\bar e_1$ and $b_2\equiv(\bar e_1-1)^d=(-1)^d(1-\bar e_1)^d=(-1)^d(1-\bar e_1)$ (powers of the idempotents $\bar e_1$, $1-\bar e_1$).

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M4 (lemma-lift-idempotent-upstairs), fourth to sixth sentences ('After replacing A by A' ... moreover b_1b_2=0'); Algebra Lemma Tag 02JK for the integrality of the base change, used there without mention

proof.text: *The element $a$.* Let $J=(b_1,b_2)\subseteq B_1$. Since $b_1+(-1)^db_2\equiv\bar e_1+(1-\bar e_1)=1$ modulo $IB_1$, we have $J+IB_1=B_1$, so no prime of $B_1$ contains both $J$ and $IB_1$: $V(J)\cap V(IB_1)=\emptyset$. The map $\operatorname{Spec}B_1\to\operatorname{Spec}A_1$ is closed [lem-weil-pbc-integral-spec-closed-map] ($B_1$ integral over $A_1$, step 3), so the image $Z$ of $V(J)$ is closed and equals its closure. $Z\cap V(IA_1)=\emptyset$: if $\mathfrak q\supseteq J$ is a prime of $B_1$ whose preimage in $A_1$ contains $IA_1$, then $\mathfrak q\supseteq IB_1+J=B_1$, impossible. By [lem-weil-pbc-separate-image-closed-from-closed] (with $R=A_1$, $S=B_1$, the ideals $IA_1$ and $J$) there is $a\in A_1$ with $a\equiv1$ modulo $IA_1$ and image of $a$ in $B_1$ lying in $J$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M4 (lemma-lift-idempotent-upstairs), sentences 'Thus (b_1,b_2)B/IB = B/IB ... see Lemma lemma-separate-image-closed-from-closed' (Algebra Lemmas Tag 00GU, 00HZ; Lemma Tag 07M3)

proof.text: *Replacing $A_1$ by $A_2=(A_1)_a$.* $\operatorname{Spec}A_2\to\operatorname{Spec}A_1$ is an open immersion [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], hence etale, and $\operatorname{Spec}A_2\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale as a composite of etale morphisms [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Since $a\equiv1$ modulo $IA_1$, $A_2/IA_2=(A_1/IA_1)_{\bar a}=(A_1/IA_1)_1=A_1/IA_1$ (localization commutes with quotients, and inverting $1$ changes nothing), so $\beta:A_1/IA_1\to A_2/IA_2$ is an isomorphism and $\alpha_2=\beta\circ\alpha_1:A/I\to A_2/IA_2$ is an isomorphism. Put $B_2=B_1\otimes_{A_1}A_2=(B_1)_a$; it is integral over $A_2$ [lem-weil-pbc-integral-base-change]. The image of $a$ in $B_2$ is a unit and lies in $JB_2$, so the images of $b_1,b_2$ (still written $b_1,b_2$) generate the unit ideal of $B_2$, and $b_1b_2=0$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M4 (lemma-lift-idempotent-upstairs), 'After replacing A by the localization A_a we get that (b_1,b_2)=B', and the general remark before Lemma Tag 07LX (composites of such etale maps are again such)

proof.text:
*The idempotent $e$.* $\operatorname{Spec}B_2=D(b_1)\cup D(b_2)$ since no prime contains $(b_1,b_2)=B_2$, and $D(b_1)\cap D(b_2)=\emptyset$ since $b_1b_2=0$ lies in every prime. So $D(b_1)$ is open with open complement $D(b_2)$, hence open and closed, and there is a unique idempotent $e\in B_2$ with $D(e)=D(b_1)$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent]. (Explicitly: writing $1=ub_1+vb_2$, $e=ub_1$ works, since $e(1-e)=ub_1vb_2=0$, and $e

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M4 (lemma-lift-idempotent-upstairs), 'Then Spec(B)=D(b_1) ⨿ D(b_2) ... Let e in B be the idempotent corresponding to D(b_1)' (Algebra Lemma Tag 00EE)

proof.text: *$e$ lifts $\bar e$.* Let $\pi:B_2\to B_2/IB_2$ be the quotient map and $\bar e_2\in B_2/IB_2$ the image of $\bar e_1$ under $B_1/IB_1\to B_2/IB_2$ (an isomorphism, $B\otimes_A$ of $\beta$), i.e. the image of $\bar e$ under $B/IB\cong B_2/IB_2$ induced by $\alpha_2$. By step 3 and the map $B_1\to B_2$, $\pi(b_1)=\bar e_2$. $\operatorname{Spec}(B_2/IB_2)$ is the closed subset $V(IB_2)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}B_2$, and for $x\in B_2$ the open $D(\pi(x))$ of it is $D(x)\cap V(IB_2)$. Hence $D(\pi(e))=D(e)\cap V(IB_2)=D(b_1)\cap V(IB_2)=D(\pi(b_1))=D(\bar e_2)$. Both $\pi(e)$ and $\bar e_2$ are idempotents of $B_2/IB_2$, so by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent] (for the ring $B_2/IB_2$) $\pi(e)=\bar e_2$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M4 (lemma-lift-idempotent-upstairs), last sentence ('by the uniqueness statement in Algebra, Lemma lemma-disjoint-decomposition')

proof.text: *Conclusion.* Take $A'=A_2$, $\alpha=\alpha_2$ and $e'\in B\otimes_AA'$ the image of $e$ under $B_2=(B\otimes_AA_1)\otimes_{A_1}A_2\cong B\otimes_AA_2$ (associativity of the tensor product). $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale and $\alpha$ is an isomorphism (step 5); $e'$ is idempotent. The composite $\rho:B\otimes_AA'\to B\otimes_A(A'/IA')\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}\otimes\alpha^{-1}}B/IB$ is, under these identifications, $\pi$ followed by the inverse of the isomorphism $B/IB\cong B_2/IB_2$ of step 7 (both send $b\otimes a'$ to $b\otimes\alpha^{-1}(a'\bmod IA')$), so $\rho(e')=\bar e$ by step 7.
